name: Juliana Stratton

issue_poll.name: Emerson College Polling/WGN-TV Illinois survey, Jan 3-5, 2026 (most important issue facing Illinois, n=1,000)
issue_poll.note: No fall 2026 Illinois issue-ranking poll found. Ranks 1-7 follow Emerson (Economy 40.4%, Health care 12.9%, Threats to democracy 12.7%, Immigration 10.4%, Crime 7.6%, Housing affordability 5.7%, Education 2.8%); 'Something else' 7.2% dropped. Emerson offered only 8 named options, so: Taxes added at 8 from M3 Strategies/Illinois Policy Institute poll of 517 IL likely voters, May 9-11, 2026 (high taxes named by over half as a top state issue; Emerson folded taxes into Economy); Foreign policy added at 9 from AP-NORC national poll, Dec 4-8, 2025 (25% name it a 2026 priority); Abortion at 10 (Emerson 0.2%; AP-NORC national 4%). Emerson sample was likely primary voters (Dem and GOP combined).

issues.detail: Raise federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $25/hour; end blanket tariffs and seek refunds of tariffs paid.
Enact Medicare for All; restore Medicaid and Medicare funding cut in the 2025 reconciliation law; lower drug prices.
Pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act; oppose the SAVE Act; expand voting hours.
Abolish ICE; comprehensive reform with path to citizenship incl. Dreamers; add immigration judges and caseworkers.
National assault weapons ban modeled on Illinois' 2023 law.
Tax incentive for below-median-price starter homes; tax penalty on hedge funds buying single-family homes funding down-payment aid; restrict AI rent-setting and tenant screening.
Oppose dismantling the U.S. Department of Education.
Raise taxes on income over $1 million to fund middle-class tax cut; reverse 2025 reconciliation law tax breaks for wealthy; expand EITC and Child Tax Credit.
Vote against supplemental Iran war funding; require congressional authorization for military intervention.
Codify in federal law access to abortion, medication abortion, IVF and contraception.

plan_caveats: Issue ranking relies on a January 2026 primary-voter poll; no Illinois issue-ranking poll near Election Day was found.
Taxes (rank 8) and Foreign policy (rank 9) were added from a May 2026 IL poll by a free-market think tank and a national AP-NORC poll, respectively, because Emerson offered only 8 named options.
Crime rated on her gun policy (assault weapons ban); her only other crime statement (restorative justice) was vague.
Minimum wage: she said $15 in 2025 campaign coverage and $25 in 2026; the later $25 figure is used.
Democracy: Sun-Times guide names the 'John Lewis Voting Rights Act'; recorded as the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
Abortion and housing positions come from October 2025 campaign coverage; no 2026 restatement with the same specifics was found.
'2025 reconciliation law' refers to what she called the 'Big Ugly bill' (One Big Beautiful Bill Act).
